newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan declines to comment on restructuring plans.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan declines to comment on restructuring plans.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp declined to comment on Monday on a newspaper report that it is planning to sell off outlets and halve its debts as part of a restructuring drive.
"It is still too early to comment on the contents of the restructuring plan, since we are still negotiating with banks," said a spokesman for Yaohan Japan.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a business daily, reported over the weekend that Yaohan Japan, the flagship firm of the international retailing group, plans to sell about 10 of its 55 stores in Japan.
It also said the firm planned to halve its debts of about 100 billion yen through sales of land and stocks in order to improve its financial situation.

The newspaper also said that Tokai Bank Ltd, with which Yaohan conducts a large portion of its financial transactions, has accepted a request from Yaohan Japan to extend a loan to help the company redeem 9.6 billion yen worth of convertible bonds in May.

The Yaohan spokesman did, however, confirm that the company had not been able to reach an agreement with Doutor Coffee Co Ltd on a plan to jointly set up a coffee shop chain in China. The newspaper report had said that the plan had been halted.
